evidence: HOW I READ: CONTEXT.txt whole, then DRAFT.txt and SOURCE.txt, the_change, the two lint findings, the inventory's general rules and every row T01 to T29 and C01 to C04. I formed my judgment from those, then opened ADMISSION.json to compare with what the writer claims. The detector results in the_change (w1102, w1102f-84, w1102f-B) are taken as reported: I did not and could not re-run them, and they are not the basis of this verdict. DOES WHAT IT SAYS: DRAFT is exactly “We’re not moving into this wound for good, either.” with its closing quote mark. CONTEXT holds it once, straight after his unchanged first sentence “I’m not going to use spiritual mumbo jumbo to shush your cries and make you forgive before you're ready.” The lead-in and that first sentence match the whole line in SOURCE word for word, and the replaced “But I’m also not going to build our whole life around this wound forever.” is gone. MEANING: both versions refuse to let the wound become the permanent condition of the shared life of the speaker and the hurt part, said to the hurt part in the first person plural (his source line already says “our”). “for good” keeps the permanence of “forever”, and “this wound” is his word, kept. The strongest reservation I weighed: the image moves from building a life around the wound to moving into it, so “whole life” is carried by the picture (you live wherever you have moved into for good) instead of being said; the pivot “But … also” becomes a plain “either”; and “I” becomes “We”. I judge these a change of image and tone, not of claim: the paragraph above states the same refusal (“if we remain in the anger forever, we are allowing the injury to dictate how we live our lives in the present”) and “moving into this wound for good” picks up its “remain in” directly. Nothing is added: no new claim, no first-person fact about Joel, no named entity. READS RIGHT: in the passage it sounds like the first half of the quote (casual: “mumbo jumbo”, “shush your cries”); “for good” and “either” are plain speech; there is no hedge, no summary and no moral, and I felt no seam where it was put in. It is short (nine words, against nineteen in the quote's first sentence and fourteen in the line it replaces), but it is still the second half of his two-sentence quote and ends the paragraph where his line did. It is a figure of speech, but the passage has others (“spiritual mumbo jumbo”, “permanent criminal”), so it does not sound like another writer. TELL ROWS: I find none actually happening, so resolved_tell_ids is empty. The closest, and why they do not count: T12 (the two refusals still pair up, but that is his own two-sided argument, since the paragraph above states the same two sides, “We cannot force forgiveness on ourselves” and then “However, if we remain in the anger forever”, so the row's exclusion for a naturally necessary contrast applies; what is gone is the mirrored “I’m not going to … But I’m also not going to …” frame that read AI); T20 and T29 (it ends the quote, but it adds the second side instead of concluding or moralising, it is plain and not an aphorism, and the paragraph above ends on a long sentence, so there is no run of short polished closers); T15 (not a near-synonym swap inside the same frame: the image, the connective and the subject all change); T16 and T18 (no “it’s Y”, no flip); T28 (stops where his script stops, no uplift); T26 (repeats nothing: “forever” no longer doubles the paragraph above, and “wound” appears once); T27 (none of his tic words); T14 (one clause replaced in place, nothing reordered, no point of his gone: see MEANING); C02 (“this wound” is the injury the paragraph above names, “we” is the speaker and the hurt part); C01, C03 and C04 do not apply. LINTER: “B7 short landing at paragraph end” on “We’re not moving into this wound for good, either.” is accepted: the line is the second half of a two-sentence quote and ends the paragraph exactly where his did, it finishes the two-sided stance the section sets up, it trails off on “either” instead of punching, and it is not an aphorism or an antithesis. “D9 follows the source order” (1/1 paragraphs, agreement 1.00) is accepted: the change replaces one clause in place, so following his order is the point and nothing is reordered; I checked T13 and T09 as the flag asks: the image notices something his abstract line did not (the wound as a place you could move into, echoing “remain in the anger” above), and the quote keeps uneven weight (one long colloquial sentence, then one short one). WRITER'S CLAIMS: ADMISSION.json has every row ABSENT and both findings JUSTIFIED_KEEP; I agree on all of it, with one quibble: the two refusals still pair up in the draft, and only the mirrored frame is broken. NOT PART OF THIS CHANGE, left alone: the straight apostrophe in his “you're” beside curly ones elsewhere; the draft's own marks are curly and match “I’m”. FOR THE CARD: say plainly that the image changes from building a life around the wound to moving into it.
